hedges.reason: OpenAI's Astra was disclosed on August 1 as its 'next major model'. A public Astra launch in September is the clearest competitor release that would push Google to bring forward a 3.8+ Flash, which is exactly the world where my NO basket on C1-C3 fails. Google has usually answered big OpenAI launches within weeks, and has often done so with a cheap, fast tier, since that is where it competes on price.

A new Claude Opus in September would be a second source of competitive pressure. The Opus launch itself sits at the frontier tier, but Anthropic usually launches or refreshes a model family together, and that moves the leaderboards Google watches. It is weaker than Astra as a trigger for an early Flash, but it spreads the hedge across more than one rival lab.

claims.reason: A 3.8+ Flash made publicly available by September 15 would mean Google cut short the rollout of 3.7 Flash, which only just arrived. The most plausible reason to accept that cost is an OpenAI major-model launch that is imminent or has just happened (Astra, disclosed on August 1). Google would move to hold price and performance leadership in the high-volume Flash tier. Without that competitive push, Google's normal pacing between Flash versions does not produce a release that early.
